name: problem solving
quote: I should do well on the test.
description: The mental process of determining which techniques can be used to effectively resolve a mental challenge.
perceptions: I'm in a situation that requires some sequence of actions.
But I don't know which actions.
I need to figure out the underlying patterns to find the right techniques and sequence.
results: Succeeding at solving the problem may result in happiness from 'winning', while failing may result in frustration or shame.
Either way, you probably learn something.

guidance.description: There are a number of solid resources to help improve problem-solving skills. Here are some.

variations.name: following a procedure
variations.description: The process of performing a sequence of steps to resolve a physical or mental challenge.
perceptions: I'm in a situation requiring a specific sequence of actions.
I know a procedure that should work.
I need to follow the steps.
results: Succeeding at solving the problem may result in happiness from 'winning', while failing may result in frustration or shame.

comparisons.description: The hard part of 'problem solving' is understanding what procedure(s) should be used to complete parts of the challenge. Once you've settled on a procedure you already know, that part should be relatively smooth.

commentaries.quote: Problem-solving isn't one size fits all. There are many ways to go about solving a problem. Sometimes you might have to try a few options to decide which works best, but there will also be times that you just trust your immediate 'gut feeling.'
Finding the best solution to a problem is a process. Remember to take breaks and get enough rest. Sometimes, a walk around the block can bring inspiration, but you should sleep on it if possible.
We cannot solve our problems with the same thinking that created them.
If the only tool you have is a hammer, you tend to see every problem as a nail.

A problem exists when someone has a goal but does not know how to achieve it. Problems can be classified as routine or nonroutine, and as well defined or ill-defined. The major cognitive processes in problem solving are representing, planning, executing, and monitoring.

Mental power is just as important as physical in the modern world. If you've never balanced a spreadsheet, your new business is likely to fail. If you've never solved an equation, your bridge is probably going to collapse. Knowledge and mental skills are important in shaping a complex environment.
